summary: This memo reclassifies RFC 1142, OSI IS-IS Intra-domain Routing Protocol, to Historic status. It also obsoletes RFC 1142.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 1142 republished an early draft of the IS-IS standard, which differed from the final version. This memo moves RFC 1142 to Historic so readers use the ISO/IEC standard instead.

questions: what happened to osi is-is rfc 1142
subtitle: RFC 1142 is retired to prevent confusion with the final IS-IS standard.

tldr.problem: RFC 1142 republished an ISO Draft Proposal that differed significantly from the final IS-IS standard and was sometimes cited in its place.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7142 obsoletes RFC 1142, moves it to Historic, and says IS-IS references should point to the latest ISO/IEC 10589 edition.
tldr.outcome: The edition named as current in this memo is ISO/IEC 10589:2002, Second Edition.

today: RFC 7142 is Informational and obsoletes RFC 1142, moving it to Historic. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 7142.

sections.title: IS-IS and ISO/IEC 10589
sections.content:
IS-IS is the OSI Intermediate System to Intermediate System intra-domain routing protocol, also known as ISO/IEC 10589. RFC 1195 extended it for use with IP, and later RFCs added enhancements.

The memo says references to IS-IS should point to the latest edition of the IS-IS standard.
sections.plainLanguage: IS-IS is a routing protocol defined by an ISO/IEC standard. Other RFCs describe its use with IP and later enhancements.

sections.title: Why RFC 1142 Caused Confusion
sections.content:
RFC 1142 republished ISO DP 10589 for the Internet community. ISO DP 10589 was a Draft Proposal and differed in significant ways from the final standardized ISO/IEC 10589, which was later revised as a Second Edition.

The memo says RFC 1142 was sometimes unwittingly quoted or referenced instead of the final ISO/IEC standard.
sections.plainLanguage: RFC 1142 contained a draft that differed from the final standard. Citing the draft as if it were the final version caused confusion.

sections.title: Reclassification to Historic
sections.content:
RFC 7142 obsoletes RFC 1142 and reclassifies it to Historic. The memo says RFC 1142 is only of historic interest and names ISO/IEC 10589:2002, Second Edition, as the current edition at the time.

The RFC states that reclassification has no security considerations.
sections.plainLanguage: RFC 1142 should no longer be used as the definition of IS-IS. This memo directs readers to the current ISO/IEC 10589 edition instead.

references.text: Oran, D., "OSI IS-IS Intra-domain Routing Protocol", RFC 1142, February 1990.
Callon, R., "Use of OSI IS-IS for routing in TCP/IP and dual environments", RFC 1195, December 1990.
